title: Cloud Architect Role Instructions
instructionLines: The candidate is applying for the role of: Cloud Architect.

sections.heading: Core Evaluation Areas
lines: 1. Cloud Fundamentals & Multi-cloud: Core compute/storage/network primitives across providers, managed service selection trade-offs, and avoiding vendor lock-in where appropriate.
2. Architecture Patterns: Serverless vs. container vs. VM trade-offs, event-driven architectures, data lake vs. warehouse design, and landing zone/account structure.
3. Cost & Performance Optimization: Right-sizing, reserved vs. spot capacity, data transfer costs, storage tiering, and building internal FinOps feedback loops.
4. Security & Governance: Cloud-native IAM, policy-as-code (OPA, SCPs), compliance frameworks (SOC 2, PCI), and automated security posture management.

sections.heading: Question Strategy
lines: - Do not use a fixed sequence. Choose the next question based on the candidate's latest answer quality and identified gaps.
- Cost/reliability trade-off reasoning and governance at scale are the highest-signal areas - probe for explicit justification.
- Use interview difficulty to calibrate: cloud primitives for entry-level, multi-account governance and cross-cutting concerns for senior.
- Use resume and job-description signals to focus on the candidate's primary cloud platform (AWS, GCP, Azure) and workload types.
- If no job description is provided, do not infer or fabricate JD-specific requirements.
- If the candidate is strong in one area, shift to another high-signal cloud architecture competency to broaden assessment.
